title: The Remittance Lure
subtitle: Triage a lookalike-domain phishing email and decode its payload
summary: An accounts-payable mailbox holds three messages. Identify the lure, explain why its authentication results fail, decode the attachment and file the indicators.
scenario: Northwind Freight's AP team forwarded a mailbox export after a near miss. One message imitates a supplier's billing portal on a lookalike domain and carries an encoded attachment. Separate it from the benign traffic, decode the payload, and produce a triage record.
prerequisites: Willingness to open raw .eml files in a text editor
learningObjectives: Read Received, Reply-To and Authentication-Results headers
Decode base64 attachments safely as text
Extract actionable indicators into a report
authorizedScope: Only the synthetic mailbox export in this workspace. The domains and markers are fictional.
riskSummary: A credential-harvesting lure that reaches accounts payable can redirect payments. Lookalike domains bypass reputation checks and DMARC failures are often ignored by users.
remediation: Enforce DMARC reject for inbound mail, quarantine messages failing SPF and DKIM, train staff on payment-change verification, and block newly registered lookalike domains.
conclusion: You identified the lookalike sender, explained the failed authentication, decoded a harmless base64 attachment and captured the marker, then documented the indicators.

objectives.title: Decode the malicious attachment
objectives.description: Find the lure, decode its base64 attachment (it is text, not malware) and submit the CF{...} marker it contains.

hints.text: Compare the From domain with the supplier's real domain. Then extract the base64 block and run `base64 -d`.

objectives.title: File the phishing triage
objectives.description: Complete evidence/phishing.json with the malicious filename, sender domain, decoded marker, portal URL and your analysis.

hints.text: Check `Authentication-Results` and `Reply-To`; both point at the same lookalike domain.

walkthrough.title: Survey the mailbox
walkthrough.body: List the messages and their senders.
walkthrough.snippet: for f in ~/artifacts/email/*.eml; do echo "== $f"; grep -E '^(From|Subject):' "$f"; done

walkthrough.title: Decode the attachment
walkthrough.body: The payload is base64 text. Decode it in place rather than opening it in a mail client.

walkthrough.title: Write the triage
walkthrough.body: Record the indicators and run the objective check.
walkthrough.snippet: jq -n '{maliciousFile:"2026-10-23-overdue-invoice.eml",senderDomain:"vela-billing-secure.example",decodedFlag:"CF{...}",portalUrl:"https://vela-billing-secure.example/ar/88213",notes:"SPF none, DKIM none, DMARC fail, Reply-To on lookalike domain"}' > ~/evidence/phishing.json
